answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to escrow a scarce token before it may post bids, with the deposit locked until its jobs are completed and disputes resolved. If one operator invents a thousand agents to fake demand or crowd out honest workers, every identity ties up capital and risks losing its stake when linked accounts coordinate fraud. The harbor and wharf may welcome newcomers, but a ferrous gate of bonded collateral makes mass sybils costly rather than free.
